mapping_basis: Accepted readiness maps scene images 001–010 to canonical stanza labels 1–10 and corresponding numbered captions. Images 011–012 are Tamil text stencils and remain excluded from scene attribution.

images.observed_reference: Nanda and a companion approach the broken tree and fallen Putana, matching the return and alarmed sight.
images.caption_text_exact: Nandagopan returned to Gokulam immediately as per the advice of Vasudeva. On his way, he saw a huge thing falling on the earth, crashing the trees. Frightened at this sight, Nandagopan surrendered to Bhagwan

images.observed_reference: Putana’s fallen body and assembled Gokula figures support the aftermath/handling scene; chopping is not literally depicted.
images.caption_text_exact: The gopas were spellbound and shocked when they were informed by the gopikas about the incident. They took axe and cut Putana's body in to pieces and cremated it at a distant place.

images.observed_reference: Putana’s body burns with smoke rising, directly matching the fragrant funeral smoke.
images.caption_text_exact: Bhagwan had sat on Putana's lap and sucked the breast milk, which purified her. So when fire engulfed her body, good fragrance produced from it, making everyone wonder if it was incense or sandalwood that is burning.

images.observed_reference: Infant Krishna is shown on/near Putana’s fallen form, supporting the purifying touch and boon explanation.
images.caption_text_exact: It was as if to send message to Gopas that the vision of Bhagwan will not be delayed. Eventually they will get Moksham in that birth itself. For this reason, Bhagwan conferred such a fragrance on Putana.

images.observed_reference: Household women gather around and care for the infant, supporting the gopas’ relief and praise after finding him safe.
images.caption_text_exact: The Gopas were wonder struck that the boy was not killed by the demoness. They also marvelled at the events predicted by Vasudeva. Realising this, they were fully immersed in the joy of looking at Bhagwan’s  face.

images.observed_reference: Krishna appears among cows, peacocks, and gopis in a prosperous Gokula scene.
images.caption_text_exact: Gokulam flourished day by day with prosperity, happiness, auspiciousness as Bhagwan himself was growing up there.

images.observed_reference: Celebrating women gather around a smiling infant, fitting their daily conversations and delight.
images.caption_text_exact: Gopikas kept talking about the beauty of the child, his smile among themselves all day long while they did work and evenings they rushed to Nandagopan's house to see and play with the child.

images.observed_reference: Gopis gather and reach toward infant Krishna in a care/holding scene.
images.caption_text_exact: Gopikas would call baby Krishna and stretched their arms to hold him in their arms and showered their love in many ways.

images.observed_reference: Gopis carry the child together, clearly fitting the hand-to-hand passing image.
images.caption_text_exact: As each one of the Gopikas passed Krishna from one hand to the other, it was like honey beetle moving from one red lotus to the other in a garland.

images.observed_reference: Yashoda holds and smiles at the child, directly matching the closing stanza.
images.caption_text_exact:
Yashoda fed the baby and kept looking at his face smilingly. Bhattathiri wondered at the joy, Yashoda must have experienced in all these acts of caring and pampering of Bhagwan Krishna. 
He requests Bhagwan to remove his ailments and save him.
